analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) G10 Spot Colour, 2) Brazil FX & Rates Commentary, 3) Thoughts on French Macro, 4) Equities Update and 5) US Midterms Webcast 7 Oct 2026
key_insights: EURUSD is back mid-range after a brief fixed income relief rally pulled 10yr OAT-Bund spreads about 30bps tighter than last week's wides. The pair still trades soft technically, and 1.1305/25 is now critical resistance.

GS FX spot trading sees no coherent exit strategy to either the French fiscal concerns or the Middle East situation. It expects few participants to take fresh big bets in G10 FX until something changes.

USDJPY is a low quality trading environment where large one-off, often macro-agnostic tickets determine daily paths. GS has pared back USDJPY shorts and watches the residual position against the top of the cloud near 159.60.

Swedish CPI came in soft, which may reduce the need for the Riksbank to keep pace with the ECB. The market has been selling NOKSEK on rallies at a 1.04 handle, and GS flags a risk of a test through 1.05 this week, particularly if Norway's equivalent print points the other way on Friday.

Brazil DIs closed about 10-15bps tighter with a steepening bias, in a more contained move after Monday's large rally. Flows on the GS desk remain better receivers in medium sizes, and CDI on/off has traded offered, indicating more inflows.
Brazil's Treasury placed in full a small to medium size NTN-B auction (about 620k dv01).
USDBRL has consolidated around 4.95/5.00 spot, and BRL failed to gain momentum despite a weaker USD. The GS BRL FX desk likes trading the mini range, with CTA and real money flows two-sided.

On Brazil politics, Flavio is seeking support from first-round losers and centrao parties. He won backing from Ronaldo Caiado and the Uniao-PP parties, while Lula has been quiet and is focusing on the 33m Brazilians who did not vote last Sunday.

Marine Le Pen's budget proposal targets €140bn of spending cuts by 2032, net of at least €30bn of tax cuts. It restores the primary balance within 18 months of taking office and puts the deficit below 3% of GDP by 2030 and below 2.5% by 2032.

The Le Pen plan has public debt at 112% of GDP by 2032 from about 121% in 2027, public spending below 50% of GDP by end of term, a deficit 'golden rule' approved by referendum, and a cut in France's net EU contribution to €5bn.

GS Europe Economics (Stott) calls the medium-term deficit trajectory a mixed bag. He credits the grasp of magnitudes and the fiscal-rule focus but is sceptical of details: the €20bn EU savings, €30bn from immigration and €30bn from tax and benefits fraud are likely overestimated, the €15bn VAT cut is kept, and the pensions proposal is omitted.

GS ETF & Custom Baskets Vol Trading (Tuteja) says the Tech/AI asymmetry has shifted. Since August 27, SPX is up 1.28% while SPXXAI (S&P ex the AI names) is down 5.19%, and the rolling 30-day return gap is near its widest since January 2023.

Tuteja says the largest SPX weights and parts of the AI story have been immune to the sharp fixed income repricing, which leaves them vulnerable to further negative macro surprises. He prefers broader market upside implementations over AI ones.

Net equity exposure remains low. GS Prime shows US Fundamental L/S (asset-weighted) nets in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback, and clients would meaningfully add exposure on dips near 7400 on SPX.

GS hosts a US Midterms Watch webcast on Wednesday October 7 at 8AM NYC with Alec Phillips and Dominic Wilson, covering the electoral landscape, party dynamics and policy impacts on yields, FX and equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Rates and oil become friendlier and index upside is driven by a broadening out of other sectors, with net exposure at the 2nd percentile leaving room for investors to add on dips near 7400.
tension_points.bear_case: The macro stays messy, so large-cap tech and AI names stall along with the rest of the market. They have been immune to the fixed income repricing and are exposed to further negative macro surprises.

tension_points.bull_case: The plan understands the magnitudes (deficit at 2.5% of GDP, €140bn effort) and the mechanisms, and focuses on a fiscal rule.
tension_points.bear_case: The detailed savings (€20bn EU, €30bn immigration, €30bn fraud) are likely overestimated, the €15bn VAT cut is kept, and pensions are omitted.
